reference.method: damped Newton at 50 digits on the README log density, from the fitted values

global.statement: With both coefficients free, a unique finite MLE exists exactly when $\max_i x_i-\min_i x_i\ge2$. Constant samples and samples on two adjacent counts have only an excluded limiting maximum. Holding $\beta$ gives a unique finite estimate of $q$ exactly when at least one observation is positive. Holding $q$ and observing at least one positive count gives a unique finite estimate of $\beta$ exactly when some observation is at least two. If $q$ is held and all observations are zero, every positive $\beta$ maximizes the likelihood. Holding both leaves only likelihood evaluation.
global.reason: The log likelihood is strictly concave in $(\alpha,\beta)$, where $\alpha=\log(-\log q)$, whenever a count is positive. The Hessian argument in Details proves this directly. Either hold is an affine restriction in these coordinates. As $\beta$ decreases to zero, positive-count masses vanish uniformly over $q$. At the other parameter boundaries the only proper limits are point masses or adjacent two-point laws. A sample range of at least two therefore forces attainment on a compact likelihood level set. The declared limits cover the remaining cases. With $q$ held, all-zero data have likelihood $(1-q)^n$, independent of $\beta$.
